title: fix(devx): npm 10 crashes with `edgesOut` on the vendor-export probe and the blank scaffold — the probe installs with a pinned npm 11, the template overrides vitest
body:
Fixes #23788

Clause-②: no

The Version Packages PR #23481 was red on two lockfile-less npm installs. Once those passed, a third install failed: the runtime image's global install. All three crash npm 10 with `npm error Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`. This PR fixes all three on `main`:

- the vendor-export `--resolve` probe now installs with a pinned npm 11;
- the blank scaffold now ships `"overrides": { "vitest": "~4.0.0" }`;
- the official runtime image (`docker/Dockerfile`) now runs its `npm install -g` under a pinned npm 11 (see **Patch round** below).

Nothing here touches `changeset-release/main`, a workflow, `.npmrc`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `pnpm-lock.yaml`. The monorepo's own pnpm install is unaffected.

## The trigger

**`vitest@4.1.12`, published 2026-10-15T14:51:24Z** under the `V4` dist-tag:

- Every other `@vitest/*` peer of 4.1.12 is pinned to exactly `4.1.12`, but it declares `"@vitest/browser-webdriverio": "^4.1.11"`.
- `@vitest/browser-webdriverio@4.1.12` was never published; the newest 4.x is 4.1.11, last modified 2026-09-08.
- The only match, 4.1.11, peers `"vitest": "4.1.11"` exactly. The peer set therefore contradicts itself.
- npm 10's arborist detaches a node while loading it and then dereferences `node.parent` (null) in `#loadPeerSet` (`build-ideal-tree.js:1289` on npm 10.9.4).
- npm 11 handles it.

Both installs reach vitest only through OPTIONAL peers: `better-auth@1.7.3` peers `vitest: ^2 || ^3 || ^4`, and `@objectstack/metadata-core` peers `vitest: ^4.0.0`. On npm 10, each resolves to vitest 4.1.12.

Bisected with npm's `--before`, npm 10.9.9, each leg in an empty directory with a fresh `--cache`:

| install | `--before=2026-10-15T08:36:00Z` | `--before=2026-10-15T14:50:00Z` | `--before=2026-10-15T14:52:00Z` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `npm install better-auth@1.7.3 --no-package-lock` (the probe) | exit 0 | exit 0 | exit 1, `edgesOut` |
| blank template, `@objectstack/*` set to `latest` | not run | exit 0 | exit 1, `edgesOut` |

The issue's hypothesis holds in kind (an upstream publish in the window brings back npm 10's `#loadPeerSet` crash). The path is different from #22912's: there the root `vitest` reached `vitest@*` through vite 8's devtools peers. Here an optional peer meets one release's inconsistent peer set. The npm side has no fix: 10.9.9 is the newest npm 10. Upstream has no fix either: re-checked at the time of this PR, there is still no `@vitest/browser-webdriverio@4.1.12` and no `vitest@4.1.13`.

## Before: reproduced

Node 22, each leg in an empty directory outside any checkout with a fresh `--cache`:

| leg | npm 10.9.4 | npm 10.9.9 | npm 11.21.0 | npm 11.21.1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (a) `npm install better-auth@1.7.3 --no-package-lock --no-audit --no-fund` in the probe's `package.json` | exit 1, `edgesOut` | exit 1, `edgesOut` | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| (a) `pnpm check:vendor-export-contract-resolve` at the base commit | exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, `edgesOut` | exit 3, same | not run | not run |
| (b) the CI step replayed on a fresh repo scaffold, `main`'s stamp `^18.0.0-next.1` | not run | first install exit 1 `edgesOut`; fallback exit 1 `edgesOut` | PASS | not run |
| (b) the same with the release branch's stamp `^18.0.0-next.2` (ETARGET, then fallback to `latest` = 17.7.0) | exit 1, `edgesOut` (template with `latest`) | fallback exit 1, `edgesOut` | PASS | exit 0 (template with `latest`) |

Isolated manifests on npm 10.9.9, for reach: `{"dependencies":{"@objectstack/plugin-auth":"latest"}}`, `{"dependencies":{"@objectstack/metadata-core":"latest"}}` and the `os init` plugin manifest (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/cli`, `typescript ^5.3.0`, `vitest ~4.0.0`) each exit 1 with `edgesOut`. The blank template with its `vitest` devDependency removed still crashes, so the template's own vitest range is not the path in, and no range change there can fix it.

## The repair, and why each route

**(ii) The probe: `scripts/check-vendor-export-contract.mjs`.** `--resolve` measures a vendor's export surface. It does not measure peer resolution. The probe now fetches `npm@11.21.0` (`PROBE_INSTALLER_NPM`, exact, at least two weeks old) into its scratch directory once per run, using the runner's npm. npm bundles its dependencies, so that install walks no peer graph. Every vendor install then runs under it.

- Failing to fetch the installer is still PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3).
- A vendor that npm 11 cannot install is still PREREQUISITE NOT MET.
- Only the npm-10 crash class stops masking the measurement.
- The verdict line names the installer: `VERDICT: PASS — vendor export contract (registry resolution, installed with npm@11.21.0)`.

Measured alternatives, not taken:

- **`--legacy-peer-deps`** also skips REQUIRED peers. `@better-auth/core@1.7.3` requires `better-call`, `jose`, `kysely` and others, and `@better-auth/core/context` then fails to import (`Cannot find package 'better-call'`, npm 10.9.9). That would be a false "does not load" red.
- **`--omit=peer --omit=optional`** still exits 1: the crash happens while the ideal tree is built.

The self-test now pins two things: the installer is exact with major 11 or later, and the probe's install argv is whole, so a flag that changes which packages land cannot creep in.

**(i) The blank template: `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/package.json`.** A user-facing manifest is affected. `npx create-objectstack` falls back to npm when pnpm is absent, and Node 22 bundles npm 10, so every such user's first `npm install` crashed. The template now ships `"overrides": { "vitest": "~4.0.0" }`, equal to its own `devDependencies.vitest`. It routes every `vitest` edge in the npm graph to the project's declared range.

- **Same tree as npm 11 without the override.** The installed tree (path plus `name@version` for every package) is identical to npm 11.21.0's without the override: 566 packages on `main`'s stamp, 563 on the fallback, 0 diff lines across npm 10.9.4, 10.9.9, 11.21.0 and 11.21.1.
- **pnpm ignores the field.** pnpm does not read npm's `overrides` (measured on pnpm 10.28.0), so pnpm installs are unchanged.
- **⛔ Not `"$vitest"`.** It also installs, but npm then stops hoisting `@objectstack/metadata-core` and nests 17 copies of it (measured on npm 10.9.4, 10.9.9 and 11.21.0; on 10.9.9, a scoped `{"@objectstack/metadata-core":{"vitest":"$vitest"}}` and a version-keyed override do the same).
- **The literal's cost is loud.** npm refuses an override that differs from the direct dependency: `EOVERRIDE: Override for vitest@^4.1.0 conflicts with direct dependency`, measured on npm 10.9.9 and 11.21.0. The new template test pins `overrides.vitest === devDependencies.vitest`, so the two move together. The changeset tells users the same.

**(iii) Workflows: not needed.** All three repairs are in non-governed files, so this PR touches no governed surface.

## After

| leg | npm 10.9.4 | npm 10.9.9 | npm 11.21.0 | npm 11.21.1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm check:vendor-export-contract-resolve` (HEAD, fresh npm cache) | exit 0, PASS, 2 edges | exit 0, PASS, 2 edges | not run | not run |
| (b) fresh repo scaffold, `main`'s stamp, the CI step replayed | PASS, first install | PASS, first install | PASS | PASS |
| (b) the same with the release stamp, `^18.0.0-next.2`, via the fallback | PASS (ETARGET, then fallback exit 0) | PASS (same) | PASS (same) | PASS (same) |

The after-PASS lines: `✓ @better-auth/core/context @ @better-auth/core@1.7.3 (via "1.7.3", 2 symbol(s))` and `✓ better-auth/adapters @ better-auth@1.7.3 (via "1.7.3", 1 symbol(s))`.

## Tests

- `pnpm --filter create-objectstack test`: 18 files, 275 tests, passing.
- `pnpm --filter create-objectstack typecheck`: exit 0, after building the dependency closure. `tsc --listFiles` includes `template-consistency.test.ts`.
- `node scripts/check-vendor-export-contract.mjs --self-test`: OK. `node scripts/sync-scaffold-emission-policy.mjs --check` and `node scripts/sync-template-versions.mjs --check`: exit 0.
- **Ablation of the new template test**, committed state first, mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with an anchor that must hit, restored from `HEAD` and proven by blob hash:
  - with the `overrides` block deleted (on-disk count 1 → 0, JSON still parses), `template-consistency.test.ts` reads `1 failed | 38 passed`, and the failure is the new case;
  - restored, it reads `39 passed`.
  - The test reads `src/templates` from disk, so no `dist/` is involved.
- `pnpm check:docs-image-tag` (patch round): self-test `118 assertions`, then `OK`, `2 driver(s) installed by docker/Dockerfile compared against 2 promised in docker/README.md (2 matched by name)`.

## Patch round: the runtime image (`docker/Dockerfile`)

With the probe and the scaffold fixed, `Scaffold with repo dist` (job 116797775725, head `c9134933e`) got as far as building the official runtime image from this checkout. It then failed at line 69 of that file, `RUN npm install -g @objectstack/cli@${OS_CLI_VERSION} "pg@^8.0.0" "mysql2@^3.0.0" && npm cache clean --force`, with the same `edgesOut` crash on `node:22-slim`'s npm.

- A global install reads no project `overrides`, so round 1 could not reach this line.
- `docker-publish.yml` ships this image, so the same line would also have broken the release's image publish.

**The change.** The same RUN now does four things:

1. Fetches `npm@11.21.0` into `/tmp/os-installer-npm` with the image's own npm. npm bundles its dependencies, so that fetch walks no peer graph.
2. Puts it first on `PATH` for that RUN only, and checks `test "$(npm --version)" = "11.21.0"`.
3. Runs the unchanged `npm install -g @objectstack/cli@${OS_CLI_VERSION} "pg@^8.0.0" "mysql2@^3.0.0"`.
4. Runs `npm cache clean --force`, then deletes the installer in the same layer.

The version is the one `PROBE_INSTALLER_NPM` holds for the same crash. The installed packages and their ranges are unchanged, and the image still ships `node:22-slim`'s npm.

**Why this mechanism.** Measured inside `node:22-slim` (node v22.23.3, npm 10.9.9, global prefix `/usr/local`):

- **Same install location.** Run from `/tmp`, the fetched npm 11 resolves first on `PATH` and uses the same global prefix: `npm config get prefix` gives `/usr/local` and `npm root -g` gives `/usr/local/lib/node_modules`. So the install lands where the image's npm would put it.
- **No image growth.** The installer is 20 MB. Deleting it in the same RUN keeps it out of every layer: the install layer is 666 MB, against 663 MB for the pre-trigger control below.
- **Not taken:**
  - `npm install -g npm@…` replaces the image's npm for every user of the image.
  - `npx npm@…` leaves 20 MB in `~/.npm/_npx` after `npm cache clean --force` (measured).
  - `--legacy-peer-deps` also skips required peers (measured on the probe).

**The gate.** `pnpm check:docs-image-tag` anchored the driver line on the first trimmed line starting `RUN npm install -g`. The new RUN opens with the installer fetch, so on the new Dockerfile the old parse went red with `DRIVER-ANCHOR-LOST` (measured). The new parse:

- anchors on `npm install -g` after a `RUN` or `&&` leader;
- drops the leader, then cuts at the next `&&`;
- does not anchor on the installer fetch, which has no `-g`.

On this tree it reads line 90 (`&& npm install -g \`) and finds `pg@^8.0.0` and `mysql2@^3.0.0`, matching 2 against 2 in `docker/README.md`. `docker/README.md` is unchanged. The new self-test cases, on the image's exact shape:

- the anchor is the driver line, not the installer line, and `npm@11.21.0` is not read as a driver;
- that shape, agreeing with the table, is green with 2 compared against 2;
- a drifted range in that shape is refused (`DRIVER-RANGE-MISMATCH`);
- an npm upgrade spelled as a global `npm install -g npm@…` ahead of the drivers is read as the install line and refused (`DRIVER-UNDOCUMENTED`), never skipped into a green.

`pnpm check:docs-image-tag` exits 0, self-test `118 assertions`.

### Readings

**Setup.** A private `dockerd` 29.8.2 in this container.

- `node:22-slim` came from the GCR and ECR mirrors of Docker Hub. Both serve index digest `sha256:c3de60bf…`; Docker Hub itself answered 429.
- The only addition on top is the proxy CA as `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, so npm inside the build can reach the registry.
- Each build used the Dockerfile byte for byte, the context `docker/` as CI uses it, and `--no-cache`.

| build | `OS_CLI_VERSION=17.7.0` | `OS_CLI_VERSION=18.0.0-next.2` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before: `c9134933e`'s Dockerfile | exit 1, `npm error Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` | exit 1, same |
| after: `d19cc5888`'s Dockerfile | exit 0, `added 525 packages` | exit 0, `added 528 packages` (on a working copy whose RUN was byte-identical; only a comment changed before the commit) |
| control: the before Dockerfile, npm limited to `--before=2026-10-15T14:50:00Z` | exit 0, `added 525 packages` | not run |

After image (`d19cc5888`, 17.7.0) against the pre-trigger control:

| reading | control (pre-trigger, npm 10.9.9) | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `os --version` | `@objectstack/cli/17.7.0 linux-x64 node-v22.23.3` | same |
| the image's `npm --version` | 10.9.9 (`/usr/local/bin/npm`) | same |
| global top level | `@objectstack corepack mysql2 npm pg` | same |
| `pg` / `mysql2`, resolved from the image's `driver-sql` | `pg@8.23.1`, `mysql2@3.24.6` | same |
| `docker-publish.yml`'s smoke: `os --version`, then `node -e "require('pg'); require('mysql2')"` from the global tree | exit 0, exit 0 | exit 0, exit 0 |
| `/tmp/os-installer-npm` | absent | absent |
| global tree (path plus `name@version`) | 722 packages | 722 packages, with 3 version differences (below) |

The 3 version differences were each published after the control's cutoff: `@mongodb-js/saslprep@1.6.1` (10-15 19:13Z), `argparse@3.0.3` (21:58Z) and `js-yaml@5.5.0` (23:28Z). Neither image contains vitest.

- **Extend example.** The README's extend-the-image example (`USER root`, then `RUN npm install -g tedious`) runs on the image's own npm 10.9.9 and installs on the after image (exit 0).
- **NOT MEASURED: linux/arm64,** the second platform `docker-publish.yml` builds. The mechanism is architecture-independent JavaScript.

## Gates (local, on head `d19cc5888`)

- **Measured tree.** The branch is behind `origin/main` (`74b436263`). On the branch tree, `dispatch-gates` flagged it as STALE: 9 of the files it derives from changed on `main` since the branch point. So the union ran on a scratch commit, `29e3f931e`: `origin/main` with this branch merged locally and never pushed. It differs from `main` by exactly this PR's 6 files, the same shape as the merge ref CI tests.
- **Derivation.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` named 96 commands: round 1's 95, plus `pnpm check:docs-image-tag`.
- **Result.** Every package was built first, under the verify lock (74 of 74 tasks). Each command then ran byte for byte with its exit code captured before any pipe, and all 96 exited 0 on the first pass.
- **Reconciliation.** `--ran`: `96 derived, 96 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- **Governed surfaces.** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --branch claude/issue-23788-npm10-edgesout` (the register on both the branch tree and `main`'s): 0 of 6 paths hit the register. NOT governed, 335 changed lines.
- **CI on `d19cc5888`** (one read at 04:27Z): all 43 check runs completed. Every one is `success` or skipped by its selector, including `Scaffold with repo dist`, `Validate Package Dependencies`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core`.
- **Left to CI.** The full farm, the 11 wide-population families and the workflow-valued families are CI's.

## What #23481 needs afterwards

Nothing is pushed to `changeset-release/main`. `release.yml`'s `version-pr` job regenerates that PR on its 6-hourly `schedule` (cron `0 */6 * * *`), or on the relay's `refresh_version_pr: true` dispatch. It does not run on a push to `main`. Once this lands, the next regeneration carries all three fixes. A re-run of the PR's bot-triggered checks is a maintainer act. A plain re-run of the existing red run reuses that run's old commit, so it cannot see this fix.

`main`'s own `schedule` run of `validate-deps.yml`, run 38843597390 at 03:03Z on `46ca793edb`, is red at the same step: "Verify the declared ranges cannot resolve past our import surface", exit 3, which is PREREQUISITE NOT MET. So this is not specific to the release branch.

## Acceptance notes

These are related findings, not fixed here:

- **`os init` / `os create` emit the same unfixed manifest class.** The `os init` plugin manifest crashes npm 10.9.9 with `edgesOut` (measured). Those emitters build `package.json` in `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` / `create.ts`, and `create.ts` is outside this claim's surface.
- **Existing npm-10 projects** that depend on any `@objectstack/*` package reaching `@objectstack/metadata-core` or `@objectstack/plugin-auth` crash the same way until upstream publishes a consistent vitest 4.x (measured: `@objectstack/plugin-auth@latest` and `@objectstack/metadata-core@latest` each alone). npm 11 installs them.
- **The template override is a hand-kept copy.** `overrides.vitest` copies `SCAFFOLD_VITEST_RANGE` by hand, guarded by the new test. A `POLICY_STAMPS` row in `scripts/sync-scaffold-emission-policy.mjs` would generate it. That script is outside this claim's surface.
- **The self-hosting guide's self-built runtime crashes the same way.** `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` offers an "equivalent" Dockerfile, `FROM node:22-slim` plus `RUN npm install -g @objectstack/cli@17.7.0`. On that image's npm 10.9.9 the RUN exits 1 with `edgesOut` (measured). Its host recipe, `npm install -g @objectstack/cli`, is the same install. The file is outside this claim's surface.
- **Pre-existing scratch-cleanup gap.** The probe's `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` exits call `process.exit` inside the `try`, so the scratch directory under the OS temp dir is not removed on those paths.
